title: [YouPass Collect] - Water consumption in Australia
prompt: The pie and bar charts below show the percentage of water consumption and use in Australia in 2004. Summarize the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The pie and bar charts illustrate the distribution of water consumption among different sectors and the breakdown of residential water usage for various purposes in Australia in 2004.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, residential users were by far the largest water consumers, accounting for the majority of total consumption, while the other sectors made up relatively minor shares. Additionally, within households, garden watering and bathroom activities consumed the most water, whereas kitchen use was the least significant.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Regarding water consumption by sector, residential use was dominant at 70%, which was more than six times higher than the second-largest consumer, the industrial sector, at 11%. Business usage followed closely behind at 10%, just 1% lower than the industrial figure. Meanwhile, water consumed by government bodies and other unlisted sources was negligible, standing at only 6% and 3% respectively, which together accounted for less than one-tenth of the total.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: As for how water was utilized in Australian homes, garden watering was the primary purpose, making up 28% of residential consumption, marginally higher than bathroom use at 27%. Washing clothes ranked third, comprising exactly one-fifth of household water usage. The remaining purposes, namely toilet flushing and kitchen activities, consumed considerably less water, with respective figures of 15% and 10%. Notably, the amount of water used for gardening was nearly three times higher than that for kitchen purposes.
